scope: invariant tangent regularization and W33 RH bridge audit

symmetry_counterexample.conclusion: Functional-equation-style reflection and real conjugation symmetry do not force zeros onto Re(s)=1/2.

claims.reason: Its nontrivial adjacency eigenvalues 2 and -4 satisfy |lambda| < 2*sqrt(11).

claims.claim: The nontrivial Ihara poles lie on |u|=1/sqrt(11).
claims.reason: This follows directly from the two quadratic Ihara factors.

claims.claim: The graph critical circle maps to Re(s)=1/2 under u=11^{-s}.
claims.reason: Using u=(sqrt(11))^{-s} instead maps the circle to Re(s)=1, not 1/2.

claims.claim: The completed zeta symmetry gives mirror phase relations away from zeros and branch cuts.
claims.reason: arg(xi) is multivalued and undefined at the zeros themselves.

claims.claim: tan(theta)=Im(z)/Re(z)=tan(phi/2) defines an invariant tangent metric.
claims.reason: This is an angular coordinate identity, not a Riemannian metric; standard stereographic polar angle depends on |z|, not arg(z).

claims.claim: Compactifying the pole at s=1 forces a stationary pi/2 boundary condition.
claims.reason: Stereographic compactification sends infinity to a point by convention but does not imply a zero derivative of phase there.

claims.claim: A critical-line zero pair has zero boundary phase torque.
claims.reason: For the natural phase of the zero-pair product, the two derivatives add and are generically nonzero even when delta=0.

claims.claim: Changing one sign makes the torque vanish iff delta=0.
claims.reason: The antisymmetric difference has that property locally, but it is not the logarithmic phase derivative of the product and is not derived from xi.

claims.claim: A nonzero local pair contribution cannot be cancelled by the rest of the completed zeta product.
claims.reason: No sign-definiteness, independence, or global cancellation theorem is proved; gamma, pole/trivial-zero, and all other zero contributions are omitted.

claims.claim: Reflection symmetry plus compactification forces all zeros to Re(s)=1/2.
claims.reason: The explicit even quartet polynomial F(s) has the same reflection and conjugation symmetries but has off-line zeros for every delta>0.

claims.claim: Mapping a positive self-adjoint eigenvalue lambda to 1/2+i*sqrt(lambda-1/4) realizes Hilbert-Polya.
claims.reason: The map puts points on Re(s)=1/2 by definition; one must prove the operator's spectral determinant equals the completed zeta function and matches every zero ordinate.
The exact W(3,3) graph-RH remains a finite analogue until a rigorous transfer theorem to classical zeta is constructed.

verdict.topological_slide_decks_status: not a valid proof in current form
salvageable_core: completed-zeta reflection symmetry away from zeros
phase-gradient language as a heuristic visualization
verdict.minimum_missing_theorem: A rigorously defined global operator or determinant whose spectrum/zeros are exactly those of the completed Riemann zeta function, together with a proof that the proposed boundary functional is positive or cannot cancel off the critical line.
